AGENDA
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  Municipal Services Building
  633 E. Broadway, Room 105
  Glendale, CA 91206
Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, iOS and
Android devices using a free app called Cablecast and choosing "Glendale TV" from the menu.
Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.
  JUNE 3, 2026 AT 5:00 PM

1.  ROLL CALL – Chraghchian, Fuentes, Malekian, Minassian, Nazarian

2.  REPORTS REGARDING POSTING OF AGENDA
  The Agenda for the June 3, 2026 Regular Meeting of the Glendale Planning
  Commission was Posted on May 28, 2026, on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  a. Approval of Planning Commission Minutes from May 20, 2026.
  1
 4.  ORAL COMMUNICATION
  Discussion is limited to items not a part of this agenda. Each speaker is limited to 5 minutes.
  Planning Commission may question or respond to the speaker but there will be no debate or
  decision.

5.  BOARD/COMMISSION MEMBER COMMENTS

6.  OLD BUSINESS
  a. ITEM:
  1137 Melrose Avenue
  ADMINISTRATIVE EXCEPTION CASE NO. PAE-005145-2025

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  This is an appeal of the Planning Hearing Officer decision to deny an Administrative
  Exception to allow and maintain an existing unpermitted six-foot tall fence and gate within
  the required 20-foot street-front setback area, in the "R-1250" - High Density Residential
  Zone, described as Lot 83, Exclusive of Alley, Casa Verdugo Villa Tract / APN: 5636-010-
  088.

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  The project is exempt from environmental review as a Class 3 “New Construction or
  Conversion of Small Structures Alterations to Land” exemption pursuant to Section 15303
  (e) of the State CEQA Guidelines because the project involves the construction of a new
  accessory (appurtenant) structure, a fence/gate.

7.  NEW BUSINESS
  a. ITEM:
  3411-3427 FOOTHILL BOULEVARD
  DENSITY BONUS HOUSE PLAN CASE NO. PDBP-005269-2025 - APPEAL CASE NO.
  PAPP-006680-2026

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  An appeal of the Planning Hearing Officer decision to approve a Density Bonus Housing
  Plan to construct a new 5-story, 209,330 square-foot, multi-family development that
  includes 87 residential units located at 3411 – 3427 Foothill Boulevard (the “Project”). The
  Project will contain 9 residential units affordable to very low-income households. The
  applicant is requesting three concessions/incentives to deviate from lot coverage, floor
  area ratio and height standards; and three waivers to allow residential units on the first
  floor, a lack of additional common open space and residential parking at- and above-
  grade. The existing automobile dealership located at the intersection of Foothill Blvd. and
  New York Ave., a one-story commercial center located in the western portion of the site
  and associated asphalt surface parking lot will be demolished. The Project site is 1.3

  2
   acres on the northwest corner of Foothill Blvd. and New York Ave., consists of two parcels
  (APNs: 5602-007-020, and 5602-007-021) and is located in the "CH" - (Commercial
  Hillside) zone, described as Portion of Lot 1, Block K, Crescenta Canada Tract, in the City
  of Glendale, in the County of Los Angeles, Assessor Numbers (APNs: 5602-007-020 and
  5602-007-021). The project qualifies for reduced parking under the State Density Bonus
  Law and GMC 30.36.090. The project will provide a total of 151 parking spaces.

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  On June 30, 2025, budget trailer bills AB 130 and AB 131 were signed and took effect
  immediately. AB 130 added Public Resources Code Section 21080.66 creating a new
  statutory CEQA exemption for certain qualifying infill housing projects that meet the
  following criteria: • Project site is no more than 20 acres. • Project site is within the
  boundaries of an incorporated municipality, or "urban area" as defined by the U.S. Census
  Bureau. • Project site was previously developed with "urban uses" or is substantially
  surrounded by sites developed with urban uses. • Project is consistent with local zoning
  standards, applicable general plan standards and any applicable local coastal program,
  subject to deviations allowed by the State Density Bonus Law. • Project must be at least
  half the density deemed appropriate to accommodate lower-income households in the
  State Housing Element Law, as set forth in Gov. Code section 65583.2(c)(3)(B) • Project
  will not require demolition of a historic structure that was placed on a historic register
  before the project's preliminary application was submitted. • For projects submitted after
  Jan. 1, 2025, no portion of the project will be used as a hotel, motel, or bed and breakfast.
  • All project sites must satisfy SB 35's site eligibility criteria (farmland, wetlands and
  conservation/species habitat areas are excluded, and coastal sites, fire hazard zones,
  hazardous waste sites, earthquake fault zones and flood areas are subject to specified
  restrictions). Staff has reviewed the project and has determined that it meets the criteria
  and is statutorily exempt from CEQA review per Public Resources Code Section
  21080.66.

b. ITEM:
  1601 WEST MOUNTAIN STREET
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT No. PCUP 006309-2026

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  To construct and operate a 1.815 megawatt ground-mount solar photovoltaic system
  (utility and transmission facilities) that will be located in a 2.1 acre (91,773 square-feet)
  area of a 219 acre city owned parcel sited within Pomeroy Canyon and the southern
  portion of the Verdugo Mountains. The Brand Park Solar Photovoltaic System Project
  (Project) is located in the "SR" - (Special Recreation) Zone. The project includes the
  construction of 3,300 ground mounted modules (PV panels), transformers and inverters
  and combiner panels extending to an approximate height of 6 feet and 6 inches (Project).
  The Project will be constructed above an inactive landfill that consists of a manufactured
  flat pad and does not involve grading (cut and fill of material); however, is anticipated to
  involve minor site preparation to level the existing grade below. The project is proposed
  on City-owned property located above Brand Park and along the existing access road.
  Electrical infrastructure will be installed as an overhead run mounted on a series of new
  wood utility poles. The site is described as V. Beaudry’s Mountains Lot Com at
  3
   Intersection of N Line of Sec 7 T 1N with E Beaudry Line of Burbank City TH S on SD E
  Line to NE Line of Sub of Rancho Providencia and Scott Tract TH SE Thereon to NW Line
  of Child's Canyon Debris Basin TH NE and following Beaudry Line of SD Debris Basin to
  SD NE line TH SE on SD NE Line and SE Prolongation Thereof to E Line of Annexation
  1938 City Owned Lands TH N Thereon to N line of Sec to Beg Part of Secs 7 and Sec 8.
  Sub of Rancho Providencia and Scott Tract as per Book 43 Page 47 to 59. V. Beaudry’s
  Mountains Lot Com Most E Cor of Block 123 Sub of Rancho Providencia and Scott Tract
  TH SW on SE Line of SD TR to W, in the City of Glendale, in the County of Los Angeles,
  Assessor Nos.(APNs: 5630-024-901, 5630-024-900, 5630-024-902, and 5630-024-904).

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  The proposed Project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Sections 15303 (Class 3 – New Construction
  or Conversion of Small Structures) and 15304 (Class 4 – Minor Alterations to Land). The
  project consists of the installation and operation of a ground-mounted solar photovoltaic
  system, including associated transformers, inverters, combiner panels, and related utility
  infrastructure, on an approximately 2.1-acre portion of an existing disturbed and
  previously graded inactive landfill pad within a larger 219-acre City-owned property. The
  project would not result in substantial modification to existing topography, removal of
  mature or indigenous trees, or significant grading. The project site consists of a
  manufactured flat pad and does not require substantial alteration of natural landforms,
  with only minor site preparation and leveling anticipated.
